relations.subject: backup:bucket-backup
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (mustUseInsteadWhen) - bucket-backup restore should not be the primary recovery method; XDCR replication from a redundant cluster should be used instead, with restore reserved for worst-case scenarios
relations.evidence: Couchbase recommends that you only restore data from bucket backups in worst-case scenarios. You should use other recovery methods, such as [XDCR replication](xdcr/xdcr.md) from a redundant cluster as the primary recovery method.

notable_absence.finding: No support-plan gate on bucket-backup restore - consistent with manage-backup.json's identical finding, reinforcing that restore uses the same capella-role:* mechanism as backup creation, not a distinct or stricter commercial gate. Also no cloud-provider-specific restore behavior on THIS page (that appears instead in the cross-CSP restore restriction noted in this page's Prerequisites, captured below) - unlike cluster-backup restore (restore-cloud-snapshot.md), which has explicit AWS/Azure cross-region logic.

cross_component_finding: This page's Prerequisites state a same-CSP restore restriction distinct from anything on the cluster-backup side: 'you can only restore to a bucket in the same Cloud Service Provider (CSP) as the one used to create the backup — such as from Azure to Azure. If you need a backup that can be restored across different CSPs, you can use a locally-stored bucket backup.' This is a real cloud-provider-driven constraint on bucket backups specifically (no cross-CSP restore without going through a downloadable/local archive), distinct in shape from cluster backups' cross-REGION (not cross-CSP) replication logic on cloud-snapshots.json/restore-cloud-snapshot.json - the two backup types have different provider-sensitivity axes (bucket backups: cross-CSP restore blocked; cluster backups: cross-region replication CSP-gated).
